prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
The 1997 Conservative manifesto sets out a continuation of market-led reform to make Britain “the Enterprise Centre of Europe,” coupled with constitutional stability and national security.

Economy and jobs
- Keep public spending below 40% of GDP, move toward a balanced budget by 2000, maintain 2.5% inflation, and aim for a 20p basic income tax rate (top rate capped at 40p).
- Protect Britain’s status as Europe’s lowest-tax major economy; deregulate further (sunset clauses), resist EU Social Chapter, minimum wage and new EU employment burdens.
- Support small firms by cutting the small companies’ corporation tax in line with personal tax cuts, reforming business rates to help SMEs, and prudently easing CGT/IHT over time.
- Expand welfare-to-work: enforce Jobseeker’s obligations, roll out Project Work nationally, develop “Britain Works,” enhance training and IT adoption (IT for All), and pass a Competition Bill.

Families, savings and pensions
- Prioritise tax cuts for families/carers by allowing transfer of an unused personal allowance to a working spouse (worth up to £17.50/week).
- Promote savings and employee share ownership; continue raising the IHT threshold as prudent.
- Pensions reform: introduce funded personal pension accounts for new entrants via NI rebates with a state guarantee at least equal to the basic pension; greater flexibility for personal/AVC savers; protect current pensioners’ basic state pension against prices.

Social services and housing
- Reform social services with more openness, common standards across sectors, user choice (including vouchers), and a national Respite Care Programme; implement a fair long-term care partnership.
- Protect Child Benefit and Family Credit; intensify anti-fraud measures.
- Extend Right to Buy, sell long-empty public homes, expand private renting, and legislate for commonhold.

Education
- Education Guarantee: national performance targets; assessment at 5/7/11/14; publish results; tougher standards in English and maths; stronger discipline; intervene in failing schools/LEAs.
- Expand school autonomy and diversity: more grant-maintained schools, selection where desired (including new grammar schools), more specialist schools; maintain nursery vouchers; learning credits for 14–21; strengthen apprenticeships; uphold rigorous A-levels.

Health and public services
- Increase NHS spending in real terms annually; cut waits; expand doctors, nurses, nurse prescribing, GP fundholding, and primary care services; use PFI to modernise.
- Extend Citizen’s Charter; broaden privatisation/competition where beneficial: consider private capital for Royal Mail while preserving universal service, privatise Parcelforce and NATS; privatise London Underground with fare caps and service protections; complete rail privatisation; expand roads and traffic management via PFI.

Law and order
- More police; fund 10,000 additional CCTV cameras; voluntary ID cards.
- Tackle youth crime (parental control orders, curfews, secure training); create a National Crime Squad.
- Mandatory minimum sentences (life for second serious violent/sexual offences; 3 years for persistent burglars; 7 years for hard-drug dealers); abolish automatic early release; strengthen victims’ protections; speed up justice; cap legal aid within cash limits; tough anti-drugs strategy.

Quality of life, countryside, environment
- Regenerate estates via tenant-led transfers and private investment; extend Rough Sleeper Initiative.
- Protect green belt; target 60%+ of new homes on brownfield; support rural shops/business; oppose a general right to roam; raise EU animal welfare; strengthen food safety.
- Lead on environmental improvement (air, water, emissions; polluter-pays incentives).

Europe, world, defence, constitution
- A flexible EU of nation states: keep veto, borders, and rebate; reject Social Chapter and federalism; embed subsidiarity; back enlargement and single market.
- Single currency: keep options open; no entry without a referendum; unlikely safe convergence by 1999.
- NATO remains cornerstone; modern, well-equipped forces; maintain nuclear deterrent.
- Evolutionary constitutional reform; more open government; oppose PR and Scottish/Welsh assemblies; NI talks based on consent with firm security.

Includes 25 pledges spanning tax, prices, jobs, small business, technology, family support, pensions, school standards/choice, NHS, public services, safety and sovereignty.
